==Biography==
Gwak "Bdd" Bo-seong joined [[CJ Entus]] as a sub mid laner in April 2015 but was unable to play a single game for them due to being underage. He finally turned 17 on March 1, 2016, and he made his competitive debut in the [[LCK/2016 Season/Spring Season|2016 LCK]] on March 2 in a series against [[Kongdoo Monster]], which CJ won 2-1. Bdd is a versatile mid laner. Despite his ability to play several meta and non-meta champions, Bdd is especially fond of assassins, citing Zed as one of his favorite champions to play.

===2016 Season===
During the [[LCK/2016 Season/Spring Season|2016 LCK Spring Season]], CJ went 8-10 in sets, finishing in eighth place overall for the spring split. [[Sky (Kim Ha-neul)|Sky]] played as the starting midlaner for CJ during the first round robin while Bdd was still underage, but Bdd assumed the starting mid position after he turned 17, just in time for the second round robin. However, it was not enough to make playoffs.

CJ Entus had a very poor showing in the [[LCK/2016 Season/Summer Season|2016 LCK Summer Season]], going 3-15 total in set score. Neither Bdd's benching and subsequent reinstating as the starting mid laner seemed to make no difference in their abysmal results. Locked into tenth place in the LCK season, CJ Entus participated in the [[LCK/2017 Season/Spring Promotion|2017 LCK Spring Promotion]]. In the first round they were swept 2-0 by [[Kongdoo Monster]], bringing them down to the loser's bracket. There, they beat [[SBENU Korea]] 2-0 before falling to [[ESC Ever]] in a 3-0 sweep to become relegated from the LCK. This marked the first time an original Kespa team was relegated from the LCK.

===2017 Season===
Following CJ Entus’ relegation, Bdd transferred to [[Longzhu Gaming]] ahead of the Summer Split, joining a roster that included [[Khan]], [[Cuzz]], [[PraY]], and [[GorillA]]. The move immediately transformed his career trajectory. In [[LCK/2017 Season/Summer Season|LCK 2027 Summer]], Longzhu finished 1st in the regular season with a 14–4 series record (31–13 in games), securing the top seed heading into playoffs. Longzhu carried that momentum into the [[LCK/2017 Season/Summer Playoffs|Playoffs]], where they defeated [[SK Telecom T1]] 3–1 in the finals to win the LCK Summer championship, marking Bdd’s first domestic title. Throughout the split, Bdd was one of the league’s standout performers, finishing 1st in MVP points and recording the highest KDA of the season, establishing himself as one of Korea’s premier mid laners almost immediately after joining the team.

At [[2017 Season World Championship/Main Event|Worlds 2017]], Longzhu entered as Korea’s first seed and dominated the group stage with a 6–0 record, showcasing their strength against international competition. However, their tournament run ended abruptly in the quarterfinals, where they were swept 0–3 by eventual world champions [[Samsung Galaxy]]. Despite the early exit, Bdd’s 2017 season was widely viewed as a breakout year, defined by his rapid rise from a relegated roster to an LCK champion and top-seeded Worlds competitor within a single calendar year.

===2025 Season===
In 2025 Bdd played the full season as the starting mid laner for [[KT Rolster]], with the year defined by fluctuating domestic results and a late peak at the World Championship. KT began the season at LCK Cup 2025, where they finished third in Group Elder with a 3–2 series record (7–6 in games). Despite advancing from the group stage, their run ended early in the playoffs following a 0–3 loss to [[Nongshim RedForce]] in Round 1.

During [[LCK/2025 Season/Rounds 1-2|Rounds 1-2]], KT recorded a 10–8 series record (23–21 games), finishing fifth overall after securing the position through a 2–1 tiebreaker victory over [[Dplus KIA]]. KT advanced to [[LCK/2025 Season/Road to MSI|Road to MSI]], where they opened with consecutive 3–0 victories over Dplus KIA and Nongshim RedForce, but failed to qualify for the [[Mid-Season Invitational]] after a 1–3 loss to [[T1]] in the qualification match. Throughout the spring portion of the season, Bdd served as KT’s primary stabilizing presence, consistently maintaining mid priority and anchoring the team’s late-game decision-making, though KT struggled to convert regular-season consistency into deep playoff runs.

KT’s summer split proved more challenging. In [[LCK/2025 Season/Rounds 3-5|Rounds 3-5]], the team finished fourth in the Legend Group with a 14–16 series record (32–38 games), reflecting continued inconsistency against the league’s top teams. At the [[LCK/2025 Season/Season Playoffs|Season Playoffs]], KT showed improvement in best-of-five play, defeating [[BNK FEARX]] (3–1) and later upsetting Gen.G (3–2). Their run concluded after consecutive 0–3 losses to [[Hanwha Life Esports]] and [[Gen.G]], resulting in a 3rd-place finish. Despite falling short of a domestic title, KT qualified for the League of Legends World Championship 2025.

At [[Worlds 2025]], KT delivered their strongest performance of the year. They advanced from the Swiss Stage with a 3–0 record, then defeated [[CTBC Flying Oyster]] (3–0) in the quarterfinals and Gen.G (3–1) in the semifinals. KT ultimately finished as Worlds runners-up after a 2–3 loss to T1 in the final. Across the tournament, Bdd delivered his strongest international showing to date as well as the most successful Worlds result in the KT organization's history.

== Trivia ==
* Bdd's name originates from his friends' nickname for him, "Boddong" (보똥).
* Known as a very good {{ci|Zed}} player.
* Along with former [[SK Telecom T1|SKT T1]] mid laner [[Scout]], was referred to by fans a "super-rookie" who would "save [[CJ Entus]]".
* Brought {{ci|Azir}} back into meta by playing it in game 2 in his debut against [[Kongdoo Monster]] in S6 Spring.
* Awarded Regular Season MVP of [[LCK/2017 Season/Summer Season|LCK 2017 Season Summer]], [[LCK/2018 Season/Spring Season|LCK 2018 Season Spring]] with 1300 and 1100, respectively.
* Awarded Player of the Spilt of [[LCK/2020 Season/Spring Season|LCK 2020 Season Spring]] and [[LCK/2020 Season/Summer Season|LCK 2020 Season Summer]] with 1200 and 1300 MVP points, respectively.
* Reached 1000 kills in the LCK on April 08, 2020
** Was the 12th player to reach 1000 kills in the LCK, after [[Faker]], [[PraY]], [[Bang]], [[Score]], [[Kuro]], [[Smeb]], [[Ambition]], [[Sangyoon]], [[Deft]], [[Teddy]] and [[Ruler]].
** His 1000th kill was on [[APK]]'s Support [[Secret (Park Ki-sun)|Secret]] in the [[LCK 2020 Spring|LCK 2020 Spring Season]] with {{ci|Zoe}}.
* Reached 1500 kills in the LCK on January 15th, 2022.
** The 9th player to reach 1500 kills in the LCK after [[Faker]], [[PraY]], [[Bang]], [[Score]], [[Kuro]], [[Deft]], [[Ruler]], and [[Teddy]].
* Reached 2000 kills in the LCK on August 10th, 2023.
** The 5th player to reach 2000 kills in the LCK after [[Faker]], [[Deft]], [[Ruler]] and [[Teddy]]
** His 2000th kill was on [[T1]]'s Jungler [[Oner]] in the [[LCK/2023 Season/Summer Playoffs|LCK 2023 Summer Playoffs]] with {{ci|Tristana}}
** The second mid laner (after [[Faker]]) to reach 2000 LCK kills.
* Reached 2500 kills in the LCK on May 4th, 2025.
** The 3rd player to reach 2500 kills in the LCK after [[Faker]] and [[Deft]].
** The second mid laner (after [[Faker]]) to reach 2500 LCK kills.
* Reached 500 games in the LCK on March 5th, 2022, becoming the 5th player to do so, after [[Score]], [[Faker]], [[Ruler]] and [[Deft]]
** His 500th game was a loss in the final game of the series against [[Fredit BRION]] in [[LCK/2022 Season/Spring Season|LCK 2022 Spring]]
* Reached 600 games played in the [[LCK]] on March 25th, 2023, becoming the 3rd player to do so after [[Faker]] and [[Deft]].
* Reached 700 games played in the [[LCK]] on March 14th, 2024, becoming the 3rd player to do so after [[Faker]] and [[Deft]].
* Reached 800 games played in the [[LCK]] on May 25th, 2025, becoming the 3rd player to do so after Faker and Deft.
* Reached 300 wins in [[LCK]] on January 20th, 2023, becoming the 8th player to do so after [[Score]], [[Faker]], [[PraY]], [[GorillA]], [[Deft]], [[Ruler]] and [[Peanut]].
** His 300th win was in the first game of the series against [[T1]] in [[LCK 2023 Spring]]. 
* Reached 400 wins in [[LCK]] on March 16th, 2024, becoming the 4th player to do so after [[Faker]], [[Deft]], and [[Peanut]].
* Reached 3000 assists in the LCK on March 5th, 2023.
** Was the 9th player to reach 3000 assists in the LCK after [[GorillA]], [[Wolf (Lee Jae-wan) | Wolf]], [[Score]], [[Faker]], [[TusiN]], [[Deft]], [[Peanut]], and [[Lehends]].
* Reached 4000 assists in the LCK on July 28th, 2024
** Was the 7th player to reach 4000 assists in the LCK after [[GorillA]], [[Faker]], [[Lehends]], [[Peanut]], [[Keria]], and Deft
